document_metadata.summary: Brian and Roberta clash over commitment; he doubts marriage and admits theoretically seeking needs elsewhere, upsetting her, while Nick watches anxiously.

entities.name: Brian and Roberta engage in a conversation about their relationship during a walk
entities.description: As Brian and Roberta stroll through a park adjacent to Harlem streets, they discuss the nature of their relationship, with Roberta expressing hope that Brian will move in with her and the children, and Brian resisting, comparing the commitment to marriage and questioning its long-term viability.

entities.name: Roberta advocates for taking emotional risks in relationships
entities.description: Roberta counters Brian's hesitation by asserting that caring for someone means taking a chance on the future, even without guarantees, emphasizing emotional courage over certainty.

document_metadata.summary: Roberta receives a card from Dorothea, whose husband is Arnold Steinhardt of the Guarneri String Quartet, and heads to violin class with Rachel after a brief exchange about the children's music.

entities.name: Roberta illegally parks her Honda and prepares to enter the school
entities.description: Roberta parks her old Honda in a restricted area, exits the car, collects her book bags and three violins, and places a previous parking ticket on the windshield before heading toward the school.

entities.name: Dorothea questions Roberta about the parking ticket tactic
entities.description: Dorothea, the photographer, calls out to Roberta from off-screen, asking in a German accent whether leaving a previous ticket on the windshield actually works as a parking strategy.

entities.name: Roberta responds to Dorothea with hopeful humor
entities.description: Roberta replies that the tactic doesn't work but says she keeps trying, expressing hope that the school might eventually give her a designated parking space.

entities.description: Dorothea clarifies that the copies are for Roberta and refuses payment, joking that Roberta will need her money for more parking tickets.

entities.description: After exchanging words about the photos and parking tickets, Roberta and Dorothea smile at each other, expressing warmth and camaraderie.

document_metadata.title: 116、INT. ROBERTA'S BROWNSTONE - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Parents plan a benefit concert with potential star performers and venue, aiming to fund Roberta's program; media attention grows as news articles highlight her fight.

entities.name: Parents And Teachers Meeting At Roberta'S House
entities.description: A gathering of parents convened in Roberta's front room to discuss strategies for supporting an educational program for children, including raising funds and generating public attention.
entities.summary: A gathering of parents convened in Roberta's front room to discuss strategies for supporting an educational program for children, including raising funds and generating public attention.

entities.name: Parents voice concerns about funding for Roberta's educational program
entities.description: Multiple parents express anxiety and frustration about the lack of financial support from the school board and district for Roberta's program, questioning its sustainability.

entities.name: Mr. Adams highlights academic success of his children in Roberta's program
entities.description: Mr. Adams emphasizes the positive outcomes of the program by noting that his son James is pursuing pre-med and his daughter April became valedictorian.

entities.name: Mr. Klein proposes writing letters to the Board and District
entities.description: Mr. Klein suggests a coordinated effort to send letters to the school board and district in an attempt to pressure them into funding the program.

entities.name: Janet dismisses letter-writing campaign as ineffective
entities.description: Janet argues that sending letters to the Board and District will not result in funding, expressing skepticism about their responsiveness.

entities.description: Isabel suggests that the parents organize their own fundraising efforts to support Roberta's educational program if official funding is not secured.

entities.description: Concepcion believes that the upcoming newspaper article about the program will help attract donations and public backing.

document_metadata.title: 121、INT. MUSIC ROOM - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Roberta reunites with four former violin students—Naeem, De Sean, Guadalupe, and Lucy—who return to perform with her at Fiddlefest, reinforcing the program's demanding standards.

entities.name: Roberta announces Fiddlefest concert participation to violin students
entities.description: Roberta enters the room energetically and informs her selected beginner and advanced violin students that they have been chosen to perform in the upcoming Fiddlefest concert, emphasizing the importance of handling the pressure and audience expectations.

entities.name: Roberta assigns Rachel as rehearsal lieutenant
entities.description: Roberta designates Rachel as her assistant during rehearsals and instructs the other students to follow her directions, establishing a leadership role within the group.

entities.name: Roberta distributes music sheets for Fiddlefest rehearsal
entities.description: Roberta has Rachel hand out sheets of music to the students, including Bach's "Minuet One", signaling the beginning of serious preparation for the concert.

entities.name: Roberta introduces rehearsal contract requiring significant time commitment
entities.description: Roberta hands out contracts outlining a demanding rehearsal schedule including weekends, weekday evenings, and pre-school meetings, surprising the students with the intensity of the commitment required.

entities.name: Students react with shock and grumbling to intense rehearsal schedule
entities.description: Upon learning the full extent of the rehearsal demands, the students express disbelief and dismay through audible complaints such as "No way!", "Before school?", and "I'ma be sleepwalking!".

entities.name: Roberta declares rehearsal regimen as Roberta String Training
entities.description: In response to student complaints, Roberta compares the upcoming rehearsal intensity to Navy Seal Training, coining the term "Roberta String Training" to emphasize the rigor and discipline expected.

entities.name: Fiddlefest Concert Rehearsal Program
entities.description: A structured and intensive rehearsal program organized by Roberta for selected beginner and advanced violin students in preparation for the Fiddlefest concert, involving scheduled practices, contracts, and leadership roles.
entities.summary: A structured and intensive rehearsal program organized by Roberta for selected beginner and advanced violin students in preparation for the Fiddlefest concert, involving scheduled practices, contracts, and leadership roles.

entities.name: rehearsal room
entities.description: An interior space where Roberta gathers her violin students for the Fiddlefest rehearsal announcement and contract distribution.

entities.name: six weeks till the concert
entities.description: A short relative temporal reference indicating the time remaining before the Fiddlefest concert, used to justify the intense rehearsal schedule.

entities.name: Roberta
entities.description: A violin instructor who leads a group of beginner and advanced students in preparation for the Fiddlefest concert, known for her energetic and demanding teaching style.
entities.summary: A woman in a guest room covers her head with a pillow, another at a window shouts at movers about violin cases, one argues on the phone in a nightgown, another questions Assunta in the kitchen, while a gift-wrapping clerk works meticulously; a woman reflects on her life, career, and marriage with Brian.

entities.name: Rachel
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students, selected as rehearsal lieutenant to assist with organizing and leading the other students during Fiddlefest preparations.
entities.summary: A 12-year-old Black girl, a talented violinist in Roberta's advanced class, strives to master vibrato, manages perfectionism, and is selected as rehearsal lieutenant for Fiddlefest, later revealing her acceptance to Juilliard.

entities.name: Carlos
entities.description: A beginner or advanced violin student of Roberta who expresses surprise at the rehearsal schedule demands outlined in the contract.
entities.summary: A 13-year-old Black boy in Roberta's advanced violin class faces peer pressure over his involvement, struggles with rehearsal demands, and uses violin lessons as an excuse to avoid teammates, while Fiddlefest students complain about time and one mocks Roberta.

entities.name: Stephanie
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.
entities.summary: A red-haired white girl in Roberta's advanced violin class is a Fiddlefest participant, involved in rehearsals for the Bach Double Concerto, and present with other students at school and practice, where she faces criticism and reacts to comments.

entities.name: Amanda
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.

entities.name: Kenny
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.

entities.name: Simon
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.

entities.name: Ramon
entities.description: A violin student who reviews the music sheets and recognizes Bach's "Minuet One", showing engagement with the rehearsal material.
entities.summary: A young violin student practices diligently despite family conflict, seeks approval, and shows progress over time while navigating personal and familial challenges related to his music.

entities.name: Vanessa
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.
entities.summary: A white girl who wears cat-themed clothing is a violin student dealing with her parents' separation, finds emotional support in her music, and has been selected to perform in the Fiddlefest concert as part of Roberta's class.

entities.name: Shandra Wilson
entities.description: One of Roberta's violin students selected to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.
entities.summary: A child receives an acceptance letter, a student discusses community deaths, and Roberta's violin students, including one in Fiddlefest, continue their music education amid program challenges.

entities.name: music sheets
entities.description: Printed sheets of musical notation distributed by Rachel for the Fiddlefest rehearsal, containing pieces such as Bach's "Minuet One".

entities.name: rehearsal contract
entities.description: A document outlining the time commitment and expectations for participation in the Fiddlefest concert, requiring signatures from students and their parents.

entities.name: Fiddlefest
entities.description: A concert event for which Roberta's violin students are preparing, involving public performance and ticket sales.
entities.summary: Roberta's violin students are rehearsing for a public music event involving performance, ticket sales, and instruction as part of a program or festival with other children and instructors.

entities.name: Naeem, De Sean, Guadalupe, and Lucy arrive at rehearsal room with violins
entities.description: Four former violin students—Naeem, De Sean, Guadalupe, and Lucy—enter the rehearsal room carrying violins, marking their return to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.

entities.name: Roberta recognizes and greets former violin students
entities.description: Roberta expresses surprise and joy upon seeing Naeem, De Sean, Guadalupe, and Lucy, hugging each of them and reestablishing a personal connection.

entities.name: Roberta introduces alumni violinists to current students
entities.description: Roberta presents Naeem, De Sean, Guadalupe, and Lucy as her first violin students and announces they will be performing in the Fiddlefest concert alongside the current class.

entities.name: De Sean warns current students about rigorous rehearsal demands
entities.description: De Sean addresses the current students, affirming Roberta's claims about the intense workload they will face during Fiddlefest preparation.

entities.name: Naeem
entities.description: A former violin student of Roberta, now a strikingly handsome man over six feet tall, recognized by a scar, who returns to participate in the Fiddlefest concert.
entities.summary: A Black boy with a scar on his left cheek attends Roberta's violin class, showing knowledge and dedication, but is temporarily withdrawn by his mother; he later returns, eager to catch up, prompting Roberta to offer private lessons.

entities.name: De Sean
entities.description: A former violin student of Roberta, now 19 years old with dreadlocks, who has a rapper-like appearance and warns current students about the intensity of rehearsals.
entities.summary: A Black boy in Roberta's violin class resists learning, claims the violin is for wimps, and requests expulsion; he disrupts class by talking, jokes about being under arrest, cites asthma for lack of practice, and questions the group's performance quality.

entities.name: Guadalupe
entities.description: A former violin student of Roberta, now 19 years old and walking with a cane, who has become a beautiful young woman with a long braid pinned up.
entities.summary: Roberta teaches a violin class with students facing physical and emotional challenges, including a girl with leg braces, a struggling beginner, and a former student now 19, who has overcome obstacles and grown into a confident young woman.

entities.name: Lucy
entities.description: A reserved Puerto Rican woman, now 20 years old, who was one of Roberta's first violin students and has returned to participate in the concert.
entities.summary: A Puerto Rican girl in Roberta's violin class improvises playfully, dancing and snapping fingers, drawing reprimands while creatively altering Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, becoming a focal point during rehearsal.

entities.name: Fiddlefest kids wait for Roberta outside locked school gate
